latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1, both fresh N=256 seeds lose their force margin to rising random controls. Force control R2 is 0.6531 (seed 23) and 0.5839 (seed 22), against N=128 controls of at most about 0.55 and 0.52 (rises of >= ~0.10 and >= ~0.06). The final force margins are 0.096 and 0.069, so neither beats its control, while accel_step clears its control easily (R2 0.926/0.917 vs control 0.715/0.756; headroom-normalised 0.74/0.66). Trained force R2 does not stay flat as predicted: it rises in seed 23 (0.7486 at N=256 vs at most ~0.714 at N=128, about +0.035) and falls in seed 22 (0.6532 vs at most ~0.696, a drop of up to about 0.043). So the control-rise half of the hypothesis holds in both seeds, but the |delta trained R2| <= 0.02 condition fails in both, in opposite directions.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.337-0.346). The paired N=128 values were not computed as pre-registered: the N=128 arm's probes_final was not available to me, so N=128 trained R2 comes from the trajectory's 4th field and control R2 from that field minus margin. In these N=256 runs that field overstates the probes_final best-layer R2 by 0.004-0.017 (0.753 vs 0.7486; 0.670 vs 0.6532). The N=128 values are therefore upper bounds. As a result, seed 22's trained drop lies somewhere in about 0.026-0.043, which straddles the 0.04 refutation bar. Seed 23's trained rise could be larger than +0.035. Every control rise is a lower bound. Seed 23's force control_spread is 0.049, so control noise is a large part of the effect. Reading N=128 probes_final directly would settle seed 22 against the 0.04 bar. A drop >= 0.04 there would make this refuted. A drop <= 0.02 in both seeds would make it supported. With two seeds whose trained-R2 changes have opposite signs, the trained-vs-control decomposition of the N=128-to-N=256 step looks noisy at the +/-0.04 level. The one robust result is the control rise.

latest_findings.claim: Fresh seeds 22-23 at N=64 on data_seed 1 have higher force than the seeds 20-21 reference: both final force margins (0.275 and 0.268) and both trained R2 values (0.809 and 0.793) are above the predicted ranges ([0.18, 0.26] and [0.68, 0.78]), while force controls (0.534 and 0.525) match the reference. accel_step stays the stronger readout: R2 0.926-0.937 at layer 4 against controls of 0.761-0.774, a raw margin of only 0.163-0.165 but a headroom-normalised margin of 0.69-0.72, versus 0.59-0.58 normalised for force. val_mse_ratio is 0.017-0.019.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither the expected-if-true nor the expected-if-false outcome occurred. Force is above control in both seeds, well clear of the 0.15 / 0.65 failure bars, but both seeds overshoot the upper bounds for margin and trained R2. The two fresh seeds agree with each other to within 0.007 in margin and 0.016 in trained R2. They sit about 0.06 above seeds 20-21 (0.209). The controls are the same, so the gap is entirely in trained R2 (0.79-0.81 vs about 0.74). The data_seed 1 N=64 force level therefore does depend on the model seed, by about 0.06, which the hypothesis did not anticipate. seeds_agree is false because the verdict is inconclusive, not because the seeds disagree. Force was still rising at step 3000 (+0.010 per 500 steps in seed 23, +0.007 in seed 22), so the final value also depends on training length. Paired context, computed from the sibling arm's trajectories (4th field, which may be max over layers rather than the best-margin layer; force best layer is 1 at every checkpoint in all four runs) and not cited as evidence: the per-seed N=64-to-N=128 trained force R2 drop is 0.095 (seed 23) and 0.097 (seed 22). The margin drop is 0.112 and 0.095. Implied N=128 controls are 0.55 and 0.52, so this step is almost entirely in trained R2, as in seeds 20-21. A matched-loss reading uses the N=64 step-1500 checkpoint (val_mse_ratio 0.073 and 0.081, close to N=128's step-3000 values). There, N=64 trained force R2 is 0.761 and 0.750 against N=128's 0.714 and 0.696, a gap of 0.047-0.054, so the N=64-to-N=128 shortfall is not explained by convergence alone. This reading uses the trajectory field and should be rechecked from per-layer probes. Two or more further seeds at about 0.21 would make seeds 22-23 look like the outliers. Two or more at about 0.27 would make seeds 20-21 the outliers.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1, fresh seeds 22-23 confirm that the force decline from N=64 to N=128 comes from lower trained R2, not from the controls. At step 3000, N=128 layer-1 force R2 is 0.714 (seed 23) and 0.696 (seed 22). The paired N=64 runs give about 0.809 and 0.793, a drop of 0.095-0.097. Force control R2 barely moves: 0.551 vs about 0.534 (+0.017) and 0.523 vs about 0.525 (-0.002). The final force margin falls from 0.275 to 0.163 and from 0.268 to 0.173, and almost all of that loss is the trained-R2 term. accel_step stays strong at layer 4 (R2 0.917/0.932 vs control 0.751/0.761; headroom-normalised margin 0.67/0.72), and layer-1 distance R2 holds or rises (0.933/0.935 vs 0.896/0.932 at N=64). So the loss is specific to force and does not reflect a general loss of the gravity-relevant code.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Every expected-if-true criterion holds in both seeds. Trained force R2 drops by 0.095-0.097 (needed >= 0.04), the control changes by -0.002 to +0.017 (needed <= 0.03), the final margins of 0.163/0.173 fall inside [0.06, 0.20], and the normalised accel_step margins of 0.67/0.72 fall inside [0.60, 0.78]. Both runs are complete (3000/3000 steps), and seed 23's force control_spread (0.056) is below the 0.1 required margin. Limits: (1) The N=64 side comes from the paired arm's rounded trajectory, not unrounded probes_final, so it is not the read the hypothesis specified. Its trained R2 is taken from the trajectory's 4th field, which may be the max over layers (q-20261013-075749-57bb), and its control is derived as R2 minus margin. The margin drop itself (0.095-0.112) does not depend on this. Exact trained and control values could shift by about 0.01-0.02, which is far from the 0.04 and 0.03 cut-offs. (2) The comparison is at matched training step, not matched loss, so N=128 may just be less converged; its force margin is still rising about 0.003-0.008 per 500 steps at step 3000. (3) Only one data_seed. The margin drop for seeds 22-23 (0.095-0.112) is larger than for seeds 20-21 on the same dataset (0.064-0.072), so model-seed spread on data_seed 1 is about as large as the data_seed 0 vs 1 difference. Two things would change the verdict: probes_final values from the N=64 arm showing a trained drop below 0.04, or a matched-loss comparison where the trained-R2 gap closes to within 0.02.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 0, N=128 still decodes force better than N=256 when the two are matched on val_mse_ratio, so the N=256 shortfall is not just slower convergence. I matched each N=128 seed to the first checkpoint where its val_mse_ratio was at or below that seed's N=256 step-4000 value. Seed 24 matches at step 3000 (val_mse_ratio 0.099 vs 0.185), where N=128 trained force R2 is 0.511 + 0.130 = 0.641 against 0.557 at N=256 (+0.084). Seed 25 matches at step 2500 (0.149 vs 0.178), where it is 0.478 + 0.152 = 0.630 against 0.569 (+0.061). At the same step 4000, N=128 force R2 is 0.656 vs 0.557 (+0.099) and 0.647 vs 0.569 (+0.078). In both seeds force beats its control at N=128 (margins 0.145 and 0.169 vs 0.10 required). accel_step is higher at R2 0.914 and 0.912 (margins 0.218 and 0.168), and its normalised margin is 0.72 and 0.66, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78].
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds clear the 0.04 bar by a wide margin, at the matched checkpoint and at step 4000. The result also holds at the checkpoint just before the match, where N=128 had a worse val_mse_ratio than the N=256 reference: seed 24 at step 2500 (0.192) gives 0.636, and seed 25 at step 2000 (0.230) gives 0.624. So the 500-step checkpoint spacing and overshooting the match (seed 24: 0.099 vs 0.185) do not drive the verdict. Main limits: (1) Only two model seeds, both on data_seed 0. On data_seed 1 the N=128-to-N=256 step was all control and no trained-R2 drop (q-20261013-092046-825b), so this may not generalise across datasets. (2) val_mse_ratio is relative to a constant-velocity baseline that gets stronger at larger N (q-20261011-225358-2acc). Matching on absolute val MSE, or on a fraction of step-0 MSE, might pair different checkpoints, although the N=128 force R2 lead holds at every checkpoint from step 2000 on. (3) The N=256 reference values (0.557 and 0.569) come from the earlier arm's probes_final, and the N=128 matched values use trajectory margins rounded to 3 decimals (error 0.0005 or less). (4) The 'trained R2' comparison ignores that controls differ by arm: N=256 force barely clears its control (margins 0.02 and 0.055). The verdict would change if N=256 trained beyond 4000 steps to val_mse_ratio around 0.05 reached force R2 of 0.64 or more, or if data_seed 1 or seeds 20-23 showed a matched-loss gap under 0.02.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-095439-b383 (issue 0): Accepted. I added layer 1's control (0.511) to layer 3's margin (0.130), which mixes two layers, and 0.641 is in fact layer 1's max_r2. Under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin, same layer), seed 24's matched N=128 trained force R2 at step 3000 is 0.6258 (layer 3: 0.4955 + 0.1303). That is +0.069 over N=256's 0.557, not +0.084. The confidence-note value at step 2500 is 0.6205 (layer 3: 0.4955 + 0.125), not 0.636, giving +0.064. Seed 25's values (layer 1 at its matched checkpoint) are unchanged: 0.630 at step 2500 (+0.061) and 0.624 at step 2000 (+0.055). Every corrected gap is still at least 0.04 above the N=256 reference in both seeds, so the verdict (supported) and the replicated status stand. Paired values in this cycle's proposals are read only from same-layer control + margin or from probes_final.

Response to review r-20261013-095439-b383 (issue 0): Accepted. For seed 24 at N=128, the best-margin layer at steps 2500 and 3000 is layer 3, with control 0.4955. I paired layer 1's control (0.511) with layer 3's margin, and the result happened to match the layer-1 max_r2. The corrected values under the pre-registered rule (control + best-layer margin) are: step 3000 (matched checkpoint) 0.4955 + 0.1303 = 0.626, which is +0.069 over N=256's 0.557; and step 2500 (the checkpoint before the match) 0.4955 + 0.125 = 0.6205, which is +0.064. Seed 25's values (0.630 matched, +0.061; 0.624 at step 2000) and the step-4000 probes_final comparisons (+0.099, +0.078) are unaffected. Every corrected gap is still >= 0.04 in both seeds, so the verdict and replicated status stand. The matched-loss N=128 lead on data_seed 0 is +0.061 to +0.069, not +0.061 to +0.084. Future paired reads will take the control from the same layer as the best margin at each checkpoint.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256, training seeds 24-25 for 4000 steps did not close the trained force R2 gap to N=128, and in both seeds the result meets the expected-if-false criteria. Final best-layer (layer 1) trained force R2 is 0.557 (seed 24) and 0.569 (seed 25), which is 0.082 and 0.053 below the same seeds' N=128 values (0.639 / 0.621). Between steps 3000 and 4000, trained force R2 rose only about 0.011 and 0.014 (force margin 0.009→0.020 and 0.041→0.055 against controls fixed at 0.537 / 0.514), and force still does not beat its control in either run. accel_step, by contrast, holds R2 0.906-0.915 against controls 0.684-0.716 (margin 0.199-0.223), with headroom-normalised margin about 0.70 in both seeds.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 4000 steps and meet every expected-if-false bar: gap >= 0.04 and gain <= 0.015. The step-3000 trained force R2 (control + margin: about 0.546 / 0.555) is within 0.017 / 0.004 of the 3000-step runs (0.563 / 0.559), so the cross-run comparison is not horizon-confounded under the pre-stated 0.03 rule. Four things limit confidence. (1) Seed 25's gain of 0.014 is only just under the 0.015 bar, and it is computed from trajectory margins rounded to 3 decimals. (2) Within-run growth comes from the trajectory margin, because the trajectory's 4th field does not equal the probes_final R2 (0.576 vs 0.557 and 0.590 vs 0.569 at step 4000), so that field cannot be used as best-margin-layer trained R2. (3) The result refutes 'closes the gap within 1000 extra steps'. It does not show a fixed ceiling: force is still gaining about +0.005-0.007 margin per 500 steps, and val_mse_ratio is still falling (0.30-0.44 to 0.18). At that rate the 0.053-0.082 gap would need roughly 4000-8000 more steps, so 'slower growth' remains possible over longer horizons. (4) There are only two seeds, on data_seed 0. The verdict would change if 6000-8000-step runs brought trained force R2 within 0.02 of N=128, or if a comparison at matched val_mse_ratio rather than matched step closed the gap.
